title: Krull topology under algebraic base extension and continuity of residue actions
statement:
Let $K\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ be fields with $\Omega/K$ algebraic. Give their automorphism groups the Krull topologies, whose identity neighbourhood bases are pointwise stabilizers of finite subsets of $\Omega$. Then the underlying-automorphism identification
$$ \operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{g\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega):g|_F=1\} $$
is a homeomorphism when the right side has the subspace topology. No finiteness of $F/K$ is required. Moreover, let $\Gamma\leq\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ have the subspace topology and preserve a local subring $T\subseteq\Omega$. Put $E=T/\mathfrak m_T$, let $\kappa$ be a subfield of $E$ fixed by its induced residue action, choose a separable closure $\kappa_s/\kappa$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and let $j:\kappa_s\hookrightarrow E$ be a $\kappa$-embedding whose image is preserved by that action. The homomorphism $r:\Gamma\to\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa_s/\kappa)$ characterized by $j(r(g)(a))=\overline g(j(a))$ is continuous for the Krull topology on its codomain. For any finite Galois $e/\kappa$ in $\kappa_s$, generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $e/\kappa$, and lifts $z_i\in T$ of $j(a_i)$, the open subgroup $\{g\in\Gamma:g(z_i)=z_i\text{ for all }i\}$ is contained in $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa_s/e))$.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ and $H=\{g\in G:g|_F=1\}$. An $F$-automorphism is exactly a $K$-automorphism in $H$, with the same composition and inverse. For a finite subset $S\subset\Omega$, its pointwise stabilizer in $\operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega)$ corresponds exactly to $H\cap\operatorname{Stab}_G(S)$. At every $h\in H$, the corresponding basic neighbourhoods on both sides impose the identical equations $g(s)=h(s)$ for $s\in S$. Thus the bijection and its inverse take basic open sets to basic open sets and are continuous. This uses no bound on $[F:K]$.

proof.text: Write $q:T\to E$ for the quotient map. Every $g\in\Gamma$ restricts to an automorphism of $T$: preservation also holds for $g^{-1}$. Such an automorphism preserves units, hence preserves the set of nonunits $\mathfrak m_T$. Consequently $\overline g(q(z))=q(g(z))$ is well defined, with inverse induced by $g^{-1}$. The hypothesis that $j(\kappa_s)$ is preserved, applied also to $g^{-1}$, lets us define $r(g)=j^{-1}\circ\overline g\circ j$ on $\kappa_s$. It fixes $\kappa$ by hypothesis, and $\overline{gh}=\overline g\circ\overline h$ gives $r(gh)=r(g)r(h)$ and the required characterization. Here $j^{-1}$ denotes only the inverse on the image of $j$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, residue action; elementary quotient and restriction construction.

proof.text: For the stated finite Galois field $e$, let $H_z=\{g\in\Gamma:g(z_i)=z_i\ \forall i\}$. This is a subgroup and is open: it is the intersection of $\Gamma$ with the basic finite pointwise stabilizer in $G$. If $g\in H_z$, then $j(r(g)(a_i))=q(g(z_i))=q(z_i)=j(a_i)$, so injectivity of $j$ gives $r(g)(a_i)=a_i$. A $\kappa$-automorphism fixing the field generators $a_i$ fixes their sums, products, and inverses of nonzero elements, hence every element of $e$. This proves $H_z\subseteq r^{-1}(\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa_s/e))$.

source.place: Tag 0BMJ, lemma-galois-profinite, induced topology from finite evaluation conditions; elementary elaboration for this item.

proof.text: To check continuity without a cofinality theorem for finite Galois subextensions, take any finite subset $A\subset\kappa_s$ and choose $z_a\in T$ with $q(z_a)=j(a)$ for every $a\in A$; these lifts exist by the definition of $E=T/\mathfrak m_T$. Its finite pointwise stabilizer $H_A$ in $\Gamma$ is open, and the same quotient calculation gives $r(H_A)\subseteq W_A$, where $W_A$ fixes $A$ pointwise. At any $g\in\Gamma$, $gH_A$ is the basic open set defined by $h(z_a)=g(z_a)$ for all $a\in A$, and $r(gH_A)\subseteq r(g)W_A$. The sets $r(g)W_A$ form a neighbourhood basis at $r(g)$ in the specified Krull topology. Every such neighbourhood therefore has an open neighbourhood of $g$ mapped into it. This is continuity at every $g$.
